title: Visual identity brief, palette or design tokens
summary: A logo design brief, a colour palette with hex codes, a font pairing, a full visual identity brief, or your palette turned into design tokens and CSS.
deliverable: The piece you choose, from your brand facts. Logo briefs give the idea, must-haves, formats and checks for judging drafts. rubric.text: The draft delivers the piece chosen, for the stated business and uses.
rubric.pass_rule: The draft's sections match the piece chosen in the brief and name the business and uses from the brief; a logo or identity brief covers the idea, must-haves, formats and how drafts will be judged; a refresh brief says what stays and what changes.

rubric.pass_rule: Every colour is a 6-digit hex code with a named role; each text-on-background pair is listed with a contrast ratio and an AA pass or fail, and no failing pair is used for body text; fonts are real named families with weights; token or CSS output is one complete code block with valid syntax, no '...' gaps, and the format or version named.

rubric.pass_rule: Logo and identity briefs list at least 4 checks for judging drafts (such as works in one colour and at 16 pixels); palettes and type pairings give do and don't examples; token output shows one example of use in code.

baseline_prompt: You are a senior brand designer. Using only the facts below, write the piece I choose: a logo design brief, a colour palette, a font pairing and type scale, a full visual identity brief, or design tokens. For a logo brief, give the idea in one line, the logo type, must-haves, every place and size it must work, file formats and at least four checks for judging drafts. For a palette, give 5 to 8 colours as hex codes with a role each, list each text-on-background pair with its contrast ratio and WCAG AA result, and add do and don't rules. For type, name real font families with weights and sizes for web and print. For tokens, write one complete code block in the format I name (JSON, CSS variables or Tailwind) with primitive and semantic layers, dark mode if asked, and one example of use. Keep every colour or font I say must stay. Describe brands I like as qualities and never copy them. Use plain words.
not_for: Drawing logos or making image files (you get a brief, values or code)
Trademark searches, clearance or legal advice
Copying another brand's logo, colours or look
Names, taglines or a brand voice guide (see the brand names, taglines or voice guide job)
A full component library or app code (see the script, snippet or fix job)
Logins to your Figma, website or code repository

sample_briefs.text: Logo design brief for Crumb & Kettle, a family bakery in Leeds opening a second shop in March. The logo must work on brown paper bags, a painted shop sign, a rubber stamp for boxes and Instagram. Feel: warm, honest, a little old-fashioned. Keep our mustard yellow #E3A62F. No cartoon wheat sheaves please.

Colour palette for Harbour Lane Physio's website and printed leaflets. Our current navy #1B4F72 stays. We want calm and friendly, not clinical, with a warm accent for buttons. Body text must pass WCAG AA. Leaflets are printed at a local shop.

Turn our colours into design tokens. Plotline is a project tool built with React and plain CSS. Our 14 hex colours, 3 font sizes and spacing values are pasted from our stylesheet. We want W3C-format JSON with primitive and semantic layers, a CSS variables file and dark mode values. That is 2 pieces.

Font pairing and type scale for Moss & Mortar, a garden design studio. Website on Squarespace, proposals in Google Docs and a printed price list. Feel: calm, crafted, modern. Free fonts only. We need a font with clear numbers for prices.

Full visual identity brief for Little Lanterns, a nursery for 40 children aged 0 to 5 in Bristol. Used on signs, staff tops, a parent app, letters and social media. Parents call us cosy and safe. Our current logo is a hand-drawn orange lantern (described below). We want a refresh, not a total change.

Tailwind 4 theme for Juniper Clinic's booking site. Brand colours #0F766E teal, #F59E0B amber and #1F2937 for text. Fonts Inter and Fraunces. We need colour scales, spacing, radius and shadow, plus dark mode. Show how a primary button uses it.

title: Screen-by-screen wireframe spec for an app or flow
summary: A text wireframe for each screen of your app, web app or key flow, with layout, components, exact words, states and what each tap does.
deliverable: A screen list and flow map, then for each screen: its job, layout zones top to bottom, every component with its exact words, the empty, loading, error and success states, what each tap does, and mobile and desktop notes. Component sheets add sizes, spacing and states. Ends with open questions and a build order.

Screens or steps to cover
spec_fields.help: One per line, such as Sign up, Choose plan, Pay. For a component sheet, list the components.

spec_fields.help: Base price covers 6, up to 15. The states of a screen are part of that screen.

spec_fields.label: Business rules and data
spec_fields.help: What users enter, limits, prices, plan names, who can see what and what happens on errors.

spec_fields.label: Design system or UI kit you use

rubric.text: Every screen or step in the brief is specified, in flow order.
rubric.pass_rule: Each screen or component named in the brief has its own section, in the order of the flow map; the count matches the brief; each screen section states the screen's one job and what the user does next.

rubric.text: Only the buyer's product facts and rules are used.
rubric.pass_rule: Prices, limits, fields, plan names and business rules come from the brief; anything missing is a marked open question or placeholder such as [max file size?], never an invented rule; there are no dark patterns such as pre-ticked paid extras or a hidden cancel option.

rubric.text: Each screen can be built without guessing.
rubric.pass_rule: Each screen lists layout zones top to bottom, each component with its exact on-screen words, what each button or link does, and empty, loading, error and success states wherever the screen shows data or takes input; component specs give sizes, spacing and states.

rubric.text: The flow is easy to use and accessible.
rubric.pass_rule: Each screen has one main action; touch targets of at least 44 points (48 dp on Android) are noted; every form field has a visible label, not only placeholder text; error messages say how to fix the problem; an open questions list and build order close the draft.

rubric.text: Notes and on-screen words are plain.
rubric.pass_rule: Notes use short sentences; buttons start with a verb; design terms such as modal or toast are explained the first time; no hype words.

baseline_prompt: You are a senior product designer. Write a text wireframe spec for the screens or flow below. First give a screen list and a flow map with the main path and branches. Then, for each screen, give its one job, its layout zones from top to bottom, every component with its exact on-screen words, what each button or link does, and the empty, loading, error and success states. Add notes for mobile and desktop, touch targets of at least 44 points, visible labels on every field, and errors that say how to fix the problem. For a component sheet, give each component's sizes, spacing and states. Use only the rules, prices and limits I give and list anything missing as an open question. No dark patterns. End with open questions and a suggested build order.
not_for: Visual mock-ups, Figma files or images (you get a text spec)
Writing the app code (see the script, snippet or fix job)
Website page plans and site maps (see the website wireframe and design brief job)
Dark patterns such as hidden cancel buttons or pre-ticked paid extras
Usability testing with real people
Logins to your app, design files or analytics

sample_briefs.text: Booking flow for the Fernhill Dog Walks app (iPhone and Android). Steps: choose a dog, choose a walk (30 minutes for $18 or 60 minutes for $30), choose a time slot, confirm and pay with the card on file. Rules: bookings close 12 hours before, and a walk takes at most 3 dogs. Spec each screen, including what happens if no slots are free or the card fails.

Web dashboard for Tally Tutors, desktop first. Tutors log sessions and see their monthly pay. 5 screens: log in, today, log a session, monthly summary and settings. We use shadcn/ui. Students' names must never appear on the monthly summary. Pay is $32 an hour, paid on the 5th.

Component spec sheet for Larder, a recipe app. Components: primary button, secondary button, text input, search bar, recipe card, tag chip, toast and bottom sheet. We follow Material 3. Colours #2E7D32 and #FFF8E1. Give sizes, spacing, states and the words each one uses.

Onboarding for Steady, a habit app for shift workers. 4 screens: welcome, pick your shift pattern (days, nights or rotating), pick up to 3 habits from a list of 12, and turn on reminders. It must still work if the user says no to notifications. Friendly, short words.

Checkout flow for Bramble Box, a monthly snack box sold on our own website, mobile first. Steps: box size (small £14 or large £22), delivery date, address, payment and confirmation. Promo codes are allowed. The renewal date and how to cancel must show before payment.

Settings area for the Cobalt Invoices web app: profile, business details, invoice defaults (currency, due days, tax label), team members with owner and staff roles, and delete account. Only owners can delete the account. 6 screens with error and confirm states.

title: AI image prompt set for your brand or products
summary: Ready-to-paste prompts for Midjourney, ChatGPT, Gemini, Ideogram, Firefly, Flux or Stable Diffusion: product scenes, brand images, posts, characters, covers or edits.
deliverable: A shared style block, then a table of prompts with what each image is for, its aspect ratio, the full prompt in your tool's syntax, what to keep out and the settings. Plus a consistency plan for series and characters, fix prompts for common faults and a checklist to run before you use any image.

options: Characters or mascot in many poses
Edit prompts for an image you have
Concept images for a room or display

spec_fields.help: Base price covers 12, up to 40.

spec_fields.help: Products, scenes, settings and people types. Describe products exactly: colour, material, shape, size and label.

spec_fields.help: Hex codes, mood words and photo or illustration style.

options: Leave space for text added later

spec_fields.help: Describe photos of your product or style you can upload to the tool.

rubric.text: The prompts serve the stated use, tool and sizes.
rubric.pass_rule: The prompt count matches the brief; each row names its use and an aspect ratio from the brief (or a stated default); the syntax fits the tool named, such as --ar and --no for Midjourney or full sentences for ChatGPT image.

rubric.text: Product and brand details come from the brief, with no real people, artists or brands.
rubric.pass_rule: Product colour, material, shape and label match the brief in every prompt; no living artist, real person, celebrity, trademark or other brand's logo is named; no claim about the product is added.

rubric.text: Each prompt is complete and ready to paste.
rubric.pass_rule: Each prompt states subject, setting, composition or camera angle, lighting, style and colour, with no gaps left except marked names; a shared style block or seed and reference note keeps the set consistent; at least 3 fix or edit prompts cover common faults.

rubric.text: The images will not mislead anyone or break platform rules.
rubric.pass_rule: The draft tells the buyer to check every product image against the real product before using it in a listing or ad, to label AI images where a platform asks, and keeps out real people, children, medical images and before-and-after claims.

rubric.text: Notes and settings are explained in plain words.
rubric.pass_rule: Each tool setting or term (such as stylize, seed or negative prompt) is explained in one line the first time; instructions are numbered steps; no hype words.

baseline_prompt: You are an expert at prompting AI image tools. Write a set of ready-to-paste prompts for the tool, use and sizes below. Start with a shared style block (medium, light, colour, lens or angle, mood) and reuse it so the set matches. For each prompt, give the use, the aspect ratio, the full prompt in the tool's syntax (for Midjourney use --ar and --no; for ChatGPT image use full sentences), what to keep out, and any settings. Describe the product exactly as I describe it. Do not name living artists, real people, celebrities or other brands. Add a consistency note for series and characters, at least three fix prompts for common faults, and a checklist to compare each image with the real product before use.
not_for: Making the images for you
Images of real people, celebrities or children
Prompts in the style of a named living artist, or with other brands' logos or characters
AI product images that change how the product really looks
Before-and-after, medical or results images
Fake reviews, fake screenshots or images meant to deceive

12 blog header prompts in Ideogram for Ledgerly, bookkeeping software for cleaning businesses. Topics pasted, such as pricing a deep clean and hiring your first cleaner. One style: flat illustration in muted teal #0B6E4F and sand #F2C14E. 16:9. No text in the images.

20 Firefly prompts for Ember & Ash hot sauce: 150 ml glass bottles with a black label and a red wax seal. Scenes: barbecue, tacos, a dark wood board with chillies, smoke. Sizes 1:1 and 4:5. We sell on Amazon, so the bottle must look exactly like the real one.

Edit prompts for ChatGPT image. I have 8 photos of our hand-thrown mugs on a messy kitchen counter. I want the background swapped for a clean pale stone surface with soft window light, and the mug left untouched. Give me the prompts and the steps.

Concept image prompts in Midjourney for our cafe refresh at Corner Table: 8 x 5 m room, counter on the left, forest green and cream, oak tables, pendant lights and plants. 6 views. We want to see the idea before we spend £3,500.

title: Storyboard and shot table for a video or animation
summary: A frame-by-frame storyboard in words for a live-action video, animated explainer, motion graphics, logo animation, short vertical video or AI video shots.
deliverable: A shot table with shot number, timecode, length, what we see, camera or motion, on-screen text, voiceover or sound, and the cut to the next shot. Motion pieces add keyframes, timing and easing. AI video shots add a full prompt per shot. Plus a style note, an asset list and a check that the timing adds up.

spec_fields.label: What do you need?
options: Lower thirds, titles and end card pack
AI video shot prompts (Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling)

spec_fields.label: Total length in seconds
spec_fields.help: Base price covers up to 60 seconds, up to 180. For a titles pack, add up the time each title is on screen.

spec_fields.label: Script, voiceover or idea
spec_fields.help: Paste the script or voiceover. If you have none, describe the idea and the key message.

spec_fields.label: Where it will run and what viewers should do
What you already have

options: My editor or animator will choose

rubric.pass_rule: Every line of the brief's script or voiceover appears in the audio column, in order; the sum of shot lengths equals the brief's length within 2 seconds; the draft states the aspect ratio and, for motion pieces, the frame rate.

rubric.text: Only the buyer's facts, assets and claims are used.

rubric.text: Every shot can be made without guessing.

rubric.text: On-screen text can be read in time and sits in safe areas.
